newsitem.title: POLAND: Bullish zloty rises vs basket, dealers puzzled.
newsitem.headline: Bullish zloty rises vs basket, dealers puzzled.

text.p: The Polish zloty jumped almost half a percentage point against the basket of currencies in early trade leaving dealers baffled as to the cause of its sudden bullishness after several days of bearish sentiment.
At 0815 GMT the zloty rose to 1.27/1.17 percent above the trading band centre from 0.94/0.86 percent at opening, breaking above the psychological resistance of one percent from parity.

"It is really very difficult to say what is causing this frenzy of dollar selling. I would have expected it on Tuesday because of the value date difference, but today?" said Piotr Czyzewski of ING bank in Warsaw.
However, the zloty then eased to 1.11/1.00 percent from the parity rate or 3.2790/820 against the dollar and 1.8790/815 against the mark from 3.2850/75 and 1.8820/35 at opening respectively.

"It may be that there was one currency sell order from someone which moved the market and then other banks joined the trend speculatively pushing the Polish unit higher," said Malgorzta Sawicka of Bank Handlowy SA.
Dealers said foreign activity on the secondary T-bill or bond markets was very small.

On the money marekt one-day deposit bids eased but offers were flat with overnight cash at 22.60/23.30 percent and tomorrow/next at 22.50/23.50 percent. The central bank offered to drain 300 million zlotys for 14 days through a reverse repo.

Dealers expect small demand at the one billion zloty 15-percent two year and 12-percent five year bond tender today on uncertainty over the government's will to impose tighter fiscal policies before parliamentary polls in September.
The central bank has said only a balanced budget in 1998 could help Poland avoid a Czech-style currency crisis.
